title: LIFO
description: Calculate ending inventory and cost of goods sold using last-in, first-out.
html:
What does LIFO mean?

LIFO means Last-In, First-Out.

The most recent inventory costs are assigned to Cost of Goods Sold first.

Ending inventory therefore generally contains older inventory costs.

Example

100 units @ $10 $1,000
100 units @ $12 $1,200
Total $2,200

Assume the company sells 150 units.

LIFO Cost of Goods Sold

100 units × $12 $1,200
50 units × $10 $500
LIFO COGS $1,700

Ending Inventory

The remaining 50 units come from the older $10 layer.

50 × $10 = $500 Ending Inventory

LIFO pattern

  • Newest costs → COGS
  • Older costs → Ending Inventory

FIFO vs LIFO when prices rise

When inventory costs are increasing, LIFO often produces higher COGS and lower ending inventory than FIFO.

quiz.prompt: A company has 100 units at $20 and then buys 100 units at $25. If 120 units are sold using LIFO, what is COGS?
quiz.explanation: LIFO assigns 100 units at $25 ($2,500) plus 20 units at $20 ($400), giving COGS of $2,900.
